clue.text: Being cut, decline fight, though voice raised

indicators.note: being cut tells us the word for decline loses its tail letter

parts.note: to decline is to fall
a set-to is a fight or scrap

explanation.surface: Someone shortening a fight, yet raising their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being cut' trims FALL to FAL; add SET-TO to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is a singing register pitched above a man's natural range, an artificially raised voice.

clue.text: Beginning to arc forward, flower opening

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of arc

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky
a flower in crosswords is a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A flower's opening as it starts to arc forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: the River Ure in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or opening.

clue.text: Given end of game, first into bath to get me under the current

indicators.note: under in a down clue places me below the current symbol
into puts the word for first inside the bath

parts.note: a spa is a bath or spring
top means first
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current
taken as written

explanation.surface: After the game, someone heads first into the bath under running water.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, extra minutes for stoppages are added at the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppage time is extra time added by the referee at the close of a match.

clue.text: Hardy character embracing aristocrat with stiff upper lip

indicators.note: embracing means the Hardy character holds the aristocrat

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
an earl is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A Hardy heroine hugging a stoical nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a stiff upper lip means not crying, staying stoically dry-eyed.

clue.text: Dismissed opener for Derbyshire seeking single — beaten

parts.note: out means dismissed, as a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: opener for takes the first letter of Derbyshire

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A Derbyshire opening batsman is out going for a single and the side is beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county cricket side; 'opener' looks like a batsman but gives just D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outdone is to be surpassed or beaten.

clue.text: Stupid problem — something to take away?

parts.note: dim means stupid
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A silly arithmetic problem to subtract from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take away' suggests subtraction alongside the sum, but means takeaway food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum is Chinese food often bought as a takeaway meal.

clue.text: Trace house in support of the community

indicators.note: in support of in a down clue puts house below the community

parts.note: EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: Find a trace of a house supporting the community.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a faint trace or reminder of something.

clue.text: Fool finds the answer in drink

indicators.note: in places the and the answer inside the drink

parts.note: mead is a honey drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot finds the solution to life in drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A meathead is a slang term for a stupid person.

clue.text: Likely to cause a slip, relative coming round — on one of these?

definitions.text: Likely to cause a slip, relative coming round — on one of these?

indicators.note: coming round says the relative surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
icy surfaces make you slip

explanation.surface: A slippery relative circling a one-wheeled cyclist.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a rider on this one-wheeler is very likely to slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-wheeled cycle is notoriously hard to balance on, so riding one invites a slip.

clue.text: That priestess's love — Leander?

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his beloved, a priestess of Aphrodite at Sestos; the clue asks for her name, and Leander himself is a brave legendary figure too

explanation.surface: Asking whether Leander was the lover of a certain priestess.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth the priestess whom Leander loved bears this name, and he himself is a heroic lover.

clue.text: Epic soap star, idle pseudo

indicators.note: pseudo means false or sham, so these letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A pretentious, lazy soap actor fancies themselves epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pseudo' signals rearranging SOAP STAR IDLE into the title of Milton's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's long poem about the Fall of Man is the great English epic.

clue.text: A shade short of experience under president

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the inexperienced word beneath the president

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was a US president
green means inexperienced

explanation.surface: A young aide working under a president.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln green is the colour worn by Robin Hood's men.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln green is a particular bright green colour, a shade of green.

clue.text: Cad getting stick about becoming clergyman

indicators.note: about tells us the stick goes around the cad

parts.note: a cue is a billiards stick
a rat is a cad or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A bounder gets a beating and turns to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stick' suggests punishment, but the stick is a CUE wrapped 'about' RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant member of the clergy in a parish.

clue.text: No partner rings in to propose

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the partner surrounds the word in

parts.note: a mate is a partner
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with no partner phones in to make a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a lonely caller phoning in, but the ringing is encirclement.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose someone for a post or award is to put their name forward.

clue.text: Free record

explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set free, and a release is a newly issued record.

clue.text: Concerned with model dating big star

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: model means to shape or reform, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gossip about a model dating a big celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' and 'big star' point to celebrity, but the star is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, late-stage star.

clue.text: Directors are all at sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' usually means confused; here it is literally afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors sit on the company board, and passengers all at sea are aboard the ship.

clue.text: Bird serving late drink

parts.note: night is late in the day
a jar is a drink, usually beer

explanation.surface: A girl serving a late-night drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' could be slang for a woman; it is the nocturnal bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird with a churring call.

clue.text: Philosopher rips top from bride's outfit

indicators.note: rips top from says the outfit loses its first letter

parts.note: a trousseau is a bride's clothes and linen

explanation.surface: A thinker tears the top off a wedding outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an Enlightenment philosopher.

clue.text: Feature wit in talk

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
a wag is a wit or joker

explanation.surface: A joker featuring in a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: A chinwag is British slang for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat or talk.

clue.text: Get smaller skirt — something tasty about it

indicators.note: about says the tasty thing wraps around the skirt

parts.note: a dish is something tasty, as in an attractive person or food
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A short skirt and something tasty around it help you slim down.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to become smaller or less, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Enter faulty cistern, ignoring cold

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged
ignoring says the letter for cold is left out

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Getting into a broken water tank but ignoring the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops C from CISTERN; 'faulty' rearranges ISTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to put in, or enter, something.

clue.text: Does class cover one?

annotationWithheld.why: 'Does class cover one?' (6): GENUS covering I gives GENIUS, but 'Does' defines nothing; the defining word is likely misread in OCR and the scan is blank

clue.text: One doing another operation, Mrs Bent

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked woman's medical operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' turns OPERATION MRS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impersonator mimics, or does, another person.

clue.text: Side making contact

explanation.definitionFit: A page is one side of a sheet of paper, and to page someone is to contact them.

clue.text: Odd number non-starter — as this

indicators.note: non-starter says the number drops its first letter

parts.note: seven is a number, and an odd one

explanation.surface: An odd number that never gets started.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVEN is odd; drop its first letter and you have the opposite, and the answer's four letters are themselves an even count.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer has four letters, an even number, so it describes itself.

clue.text: Indian state in the country, way out east, a restricted territory

indicators.note: in places the Indian state inside the shortened country
way out tells us the word way is removed

parts.note: Norway is the country
Goa is a state of India

explanation.surface: An Indian region amid a nation, way out east, is off-limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a far-eastern location, but east is just the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a district where entry is forbidden or dangerous.

clue.text: A bloomer say to back leaderless element

indicators.note: to back means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is say

indicators.note: leaderless removes the element's first letter

parts.note: uranium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A gaffe made by backing a headless element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A geranium is a flowering garden plant, so it blooms.
